sections.h2: How can a Taylor homeowner sell without a long wait?
sections.html:
A Taylor owner may hire an agent, locate a buyer privately, or accept cash from someone willing to take the house as it stands. The house itself often decides, since Downriver neighborhoods like Taylor hold many older, modestly priced homes where repair bills can exceed what owners expected.

Taylor's median home value is $152,600 in Census figures, and 18.4% of residents live in poverty. An owner whose roof or furnace has failed may have no savings left to fix it first, and a direct purchase of the house as is becomes worth a look.

  • Agent listing: strongest price potential when the house shows well and a financed buyer can be waited out.
  • Do it yourself: saves the commission, yet you still need a purchase agreement, title work and a recorded deed.
  • Cash sale: no repairs or open houses, with the closing date negotiated in the contract.

One Taylor rule affects every route: the city wants a certificate of occupancy whenever ownership changes, as explained below.

sections.h2: What is Taylor like, and where does it sit?
sections.html:
Taylor spans about 23.6 square miles of Wayne County, and the 2025 Census estimate is 61,279 people. Dearborn Heights is its northern neighbor, and Allen Park and Southgate touch its eastern line. I-94 passes through the north end, I-75 clips the southeast, and Telegraph Road (US 24) serves as the main spine.

Peter Coan bought the first parcel from the federal government in 1830, and residents carved out Taylor Township in 1847, naming it for Zachary Taylor. A railroad stop built in 1876 became known as Hand Corners. Voters chose cityhood in November 1966, and the charter won approval on March 6, 1968. Southland Shopping Center arrived in 1970 at Eureka and Pardee roads, and Trader's Pointe opened in June 2018 on the old Gibraltar Trade Center site.

Heritage Park, with Coan Lake, a near replica of the old train station and the relocated 1882 West Mound church building, is a local draw. The Downriver campus of Wayne County Community College District is on Northline Road.

sections.h2: Which Census figures matter to Taylor sellers?
sections.html:
Buyer budgets drive this market. Two of every three homes have owner occupants, and the typical value trails Sterling Heights, Troy and Walker by a wide margin.

sections.h2: Does Taylor require a certificate of occupancy when a house is sold?
sections.html:
Yes. Under Zoning Ordinance Section 25.06, the Building Department says, ownership changes call for a certificate of occupancy before anyone moves in. One certificate covers a single owner's time holding the house and does not pass to the next buyer.

This matters when you accept a fast offer. If the buyer cannot move in until the city issues the certificate, a repair item raised in the inspection can hold up occupancy. Ask the Building Department at 734-287-6550 what an inspector will check, and whether anything on the house could fail. The department is at 23555 Goddard Road, and its building inspectors keep short office hours each weekday morning and late afternoon.

Exterior work such as fences, siding, windows, roofing and concrete needs a permit, as does interior work that changes structure. Painting, tile and carpet do not. The city says no work can start until a permit has been issued, so pull permits for any repair you make before closing.

sections.h2: What should a Taylor seller line up in the first week?
sections.html:
Begin with a few calls and one printout. A short list keeps a quick sale moving.

  • Print the current tax bill from the city's online tax lookup, which shows the balance and any penalty.
  • Call the Building Department at 734-287-6550 about the certificate of occupancy and any open permits.
  • Request a lender payoff letter when a mortgage remains.
  • Collect the lease and rental certificate if tenants live in the house.
  • Choose whether a title company or an attorney will prepare the deed for the Wayne County Register of Deeds.

Each task is small, and together they head off most surprises in a buyer's title search.

sections.h2: What do rented houses in Taylor need before a sale?
sections.html:
Rental houses carry their own paperwork. City code Article V, Sections 8-100 through 8-111, calls for registration and a rental certificate of compliance, which stays valid three years and must be renewed before it lapses. Fines run $150 for a first violation, $250 for a second and $500 afterward, and each day can count separately.

Give a buyer both the lease and the current certificate. A new owner inherits the same duties, so a missing certificate becomes that owner's first expense.

sections.h2: What stands out about Taylor's economy and schools?
sections.html:
Shopping is a visible part of the local economy. The Census Bureau reports $1.71 billion in retail sales for 2022, or $27,683 per resident, and the Eureka Road corridor around Southland Shopping Center holds a large part of it. Masco, founded in Taylor in 1929, moved its headquarters out around 2015, and its former property was leased by Ford. Heritage Hospital and the Wayne County Community College District's Downriver campus add jobs and students.

The Taylor School District has a single comprehensive high school, Taylor High on Beech Daly Road. Charter options include Taylor Preparatory High School, Taylor Exemplar Academy and Trillium Academy. Municipal buildings cluster along Goddard Road near Telegraph, and Northline Road leads to the college and the south entrance of Heritage Park.

Other Census items worth knowing: 19.2% of residents are Black, 7.6% are Hispanic or Latino, 12.1% of people under 65 have a disability, and 2,922 residents are veterans.

sections.h2: What transfer tax and recording costs come with a Taylor sale?
sections.html:
Wayne County states its levies on the register's page: county $0.55 and state $3.75, each per $500 of the price. The grantor pays them when the deed is recorded, and MCL 207.523 names the seller as liable. A deed qualifying for an exemption skips the tax, provided it cites the lettered subsection of MCL 207.526 or MCL 207.505.

Recording itself costs $30.00 per document since January 1, 2026: a $26.00 fee and a $4.00 state survey and remonumentation charge. Warranty deeds need a Wayne County Treasurer tax certification beforehand. The recording desk answers at (313) 224-5851, and the office suggests having an attorney prepare the deed.

sections.h2: How do Taylor tax bills work around a closing?
sections.html:
The summer bill is due September 30, and the winter bill falls due in mid-February. A real property balance still open on March 1 goes to the Wayne County Treasurer, and a second unpaid year exposes the house to tax foreclosure. Taylor cuts the summer bill along a July 1 to June 30 year and the winter bill along December 1 to November 30, so closing proration follows those periods.

Homeowners 62 or older whose income stayed below $40,000 can defer the summer bill by applying before September 30. Delinquent water charges and unpaid ordinance citations may be added to a bill as special assessments. Michigan Treasury says taxable value uncaps in the calendar year after a transfer, so a buyer should plan for a larger bill. The assessor's number is 734-374-1315.

faqs.q: Is an inspection part of selling in Taylor?
faqs.a: The city issues a certificate of occupancy to the new owner after any ownership change, and the Building Department at 734-287-6550 can explain what its inspector looks at.

faqs.q: What is the Wayne County cost to record a deed?
faqs.a: A flat $30.00 per document, effective January 1, 2026. Transfer tax comes on top unless the deed is exempt.

faqs.q: Does the buyer or the seller owe Taylor transfer tax?
faqs.a: The statute puts it on the seller. A purchase agreement can assign it to the buyer by agreement.

faqs.q: What if taxes are late when I sell my Taylor house?
faqs.a: After March 1 the balance sits with the county treasurer, and the title agent deducts what is owed from your proceeds at closing.

faqs.q: Are rented houses treated differently in Taylor?
faqs.a: Yes. They need registration and a three-year certificate of compliance, with fines starting at $150 for a violation.
